The SSME/STAEBL code is a stand-alone structural optimization code for the automated design of SSME turbopump blades.
The SSME/STAEBL code was developed by systematically modifying and enhancing the STAEBL (Structural Tailoring of Engine Blades) code.
The key design variables considered in the SSME blade optimization include blade thickness distribution, root chord, and blade cross-section stacking offsets.
The optimization considers centrifugal, thermal, and pressure loads, as well as constraints such as resonance margins, root stress, tip displacement, and forced vibration response.
Accounting for temperature-dependent material properties can require additional weight in the optimal design, mainly due to a reduction in yield stress.
For the blade designs dominated by root stress constraints, the crystal axis orientation was found to be a relatively unimportant design variable.
The blade cross-section stacking offsets were shown to have a very significant effect on the optimal design, especially for designs dominated by root stress constraints.

The additions and modifications to the STAEBL code include thermal stress analysis, gas dynamic (pressure) loads, temperature-dependent material and thermal properties, forced vibrations, tip displacement constraints, single-crystal material analysis, blade cross-section stacking offsets, and a direct time integration algorithm for transient dynamic response.

Optimization studies found that accounting for thermal and pressure loads, as well as temperature-dependent properties, can require additional weight in the optimal design compared to designs optimized under centrifugal loads only.

The single-crystal blade optimization study showed that the crystal axis orientation was a relatively unimportant design variable, with the optimal design being determined primarily by the geometric design variables.
The SSME/STAEBL code includes capabilities for data transfer from finite element models and stand-alone analysis.
Several design optimization studies have been completed using an SSME blade design to test the various capabilities of the SSME/STAEBL code.
The optimization studies were dominated mainly by root stress constraints, which were found to be extremely sensitive to blade cross-section stacking offsets.
The optimized design recommended a significant change in blade cross-section stacking to meet the root stress constraint.
The structural optimization approach provides a practical and flexible way to address the SSME blade design problem, which involves a large number of potentially conflicting constraints.
